game.title: The Darkness (2007)
game.renderer: Direct3D 12 via ReXGlue (Xenia-derived Xenos GPU emulation)
game.platform: Windows - OUR OWN static recompilation of the Xbox 360 disc (ReXGlue SDK v0.10.0), not an official PC release
game.notes: Project: github.com/TefMeister/the-darkness-vr. Process is darknessrecomp.exe with rexruntime.dll + rexgpu-xenos.dll + TracyClient.dll and an Assets\ junction to the extracted disc. There has never been a PC version, so every route below was worked out against this recompiled build and may not transfer to any other port.

api_notes: VIRTUAL XBOX 360 PAD WORKS. ViGEmBus (Nefarius, running) driven from Python with the vgamepad package. START and A navigate the menus; the RIGHT STICK turns the camera. Create the pad BEFORE launching the game so SDL sees it at initialisation. [verified-live 2026-09-16, n=3 runs for menus, n=1 run for look]
The build's input backend is SDL (input_backend = 'sdl').

THE PAD ROUTE APPEARS TO NEED THE GAME WINDOW FOCUSED. A diagnostic run with Microsoft Edge in front for all 135 s: the menu presses did nothing, memory never rose past ~680 MB (a level needs ~1.1 GB) and the idle trailer played. Every run that reached gameplay had the game focused. Consistent with SDL ignoring game controllers while unfocused by default. [verified-live 2026-09-16, n=1 failing vs n=3 succeeding - correlational, not proven]. An SDK option, input_background_events = true in darknessrecomp.toml, sets SDL_HINT_JOYSTICK_ALLOW_BACKGROUND_EVENTS before the gamepad subsystem starts; it is built and switched on but UNPROVEN - in its one run the game took focus by itself. Until proven, bring the game window to the front before driving it.

NOT TESTED: the keyboard route. The SDK maps keys to pad buttons by default even with mnk_mode = false - keybind_start = 'X', keybind_a = 'Semicolon', keybind_back = 'Z', keybind_dpad_down = 'Shift+Down' (defaults read from the SDK source). Untried on this game.

LOOK SPEED RAMPS. A short, small nudge (right stick 0.55 for 0.35 s) produced NO visible turn at all, even by eye; full deflection for 0.8 s turned it clearly. Do not read a null from a short nudge as 'look is disabled'. [verified-live 2026-09-16, n=1 each]

states.name: intro_logos
states.detect: Pre-rendered WMV logos: moon over a starfield (~10 s), then storm clouds, crows and the Union Entertainment logo (~20 s). Chain is logo_topcow -> logo_union -> logo_2k -> logo_sbz (Content/Gui/CubeWnd.xcr).

states.name: title_screen
states.detect: 'THE DARKNESS' lettering over dark tendril textures with warm light blooms, reached ~70 s after launch following a black frame and a ~180 MB memory jump at ~50 s.

states.name: attract_trailer
states.detect: Plays AUTOMATICALLY after the menu sits idle - Content/Videos/Wmv/DarknessAttractionVideo.wmv opened at ~94 s in a verbose log. Shows cinematic shots including a 'BUTCHER JOYCE' character name card over a lit close-up. LOOKS LIKE GAMEPLAY AND IS NOT.
states.notes: Distinguish it from real gameplay by a verbose log (log_verbose = true) - the trailer opens the .wmv and no level file; real gameplay opens NY1_* level files.

states.name: level_loading
states.detect: Black window; memory climbs from ~630 MB to ~1.1 GB (t ~80-100 s after the menu presses). Verbose log resolves NY1_Tunnel_00001010.XDF, NY1_Tunnel_00001010_Load.XDF, NY1_Tunnel_Common.XDF, NY1_Tunnel_Precache.XDF.

states.name: gameplay_car_opening
states.detect: First-person: Jackie's hands in the back of a moving car, tutorial prompt 'Use to look around' with two thumbstick icons, lighting sweeping as tunnel lights pass. Later the full car chase: driver, gesturing passenger, tunnel, traffic, dust particles, opening cast credits (e.g. 'Lauren Ambrose').
states.notes: The camera starts pointed DOWN at the hands. The look stick works here. The first-person hands framing is fixed until the stick moves, so it is a good stable state for input tests - but the car is moving, so compare frames a fraction of a second apart, not seconds apart.

states.name: main_menu
states.detect: CONTINUE / NEW GAME / CHECKPOINTS / MULTIPLAYER / OPTIONS / EXTRA CONTENT, stacked centre-screen over the dark skin texture. CONTINUE is highlighted on arrival.

states.name: save_notice_dialogue
states.detect: A cassette icon over 'When this icon is displayed game content is being saved...' with a single OK button. Appears after the FIRST START press, before the main menu. A is needed to dismiss it; X and Space do nothing here.

steps: create the virtual Xbox 360 pad first (vgamepad.VX360Gamepad), then launch darknessrecomp.exe with the build folder as the working directory
wait for the process; time everything from the moment it appears
press START at 55 s, A at 60 s and 65 s, START at 70 s, A at 75, 80, 85 and 90 s (each press held 0.15 s)
the level loads ~80-100 s; gameplay is visible by ~105-110 s
routes.notes: n=3 runs, identical outcome. The presses MUST land before ~94 s, when the idle attract trailer starts. The route is timing-based, not state-verified - a slower machine or a changed intro would shift it. Driver: the-darkness-vr/dev-archive/build-scripts/padpress.py and looktest.py. 2026-09-16: FAILED once when Microsoft Edge held focus for the whole run - the presses did not register and the trailer played. Treat 'game window focused' as a precondition.

DISPROVED as a working route - KEPT so it is not retried blind. The config IS read (verbose log resolves D:\EnvironmentXbox.cfg) and the game DOES skip the videos and go to world loading, but about one second later it hits a deliberate debug break (0x80000003 in rexruntime.dll at +0xAB8B0, an int3;ret helper) with no message logged. A control run without the file survives. Two causes ruled out: missing .xw world files and the missing MONOPRO.XFC font are both absent in the WORKING run too. Currently disabled as EnvironmentXbox.cfg.off.

routes.how: START (pad) -> save_notice_dialogue -> A -> title 'PRESS START' again -> START -> main_menu. The dialogue in the middle is easy to miss; a single START does NOT reach the menu.
routes.notes: Timing that worked, measured from launch: title visible ~70 s, START 74 s, A 78 s, START 82 s, menu up by 86 s.

config_files: darknessrecomp.toml beside the exe - ReXGlue cvars (fullscreen, window size, resolution_scale, log_verbose, log_flush_interval ...). Read at start.
Assets\EnvironmentXbox.cfg (falls back to Environment.cfg) - the engine's ENV settings, e.g. QUICKMAP / QUICKMENU / COMMANDLINE. Not shipped on the disc.
entry_points.logs: logs\darknessrecomp_NNN.log beside the exe. By default only FAILED file opens are logged; log_verbose = true plus log_flush_interval = 1 records every successful open too (slows the game, ~26 MB in a few minutes).

commands.console: NONE FOUND. The engine's ENV settings (QUICKMAP, QUICKMENU, and a COMMANDLINE key accepting -MAP <name>, -DEMO, -EXEC) are the only command-like route identified, from disassembly, and QUICKMAP traps as above. [inferred-static + verified-live 2026-09-16]

hazards.hazard: The idle attract trailer masquerades as gameplay
hazards.notes: A hands-off run left at the menu reaches a 'BUTCHER JOYCE' character card that looks in-engine. It is DarknessAttractionVideo.wmv. A session concluded 'probably real 3D' from it before a verbose log proved otherwise. Always confirm gameplay by a level file (NY1_*) opening, not by the look of a frame.

hazards.hazard: Whole-frame image comparison is pinned at zero by the fixed HUD prompt
hazards.notes: The 'Use to look around' prompt never moves, so whole-frame phase correlation reports no shift even while the camera turns. Measure a region that excludes the HUD (the lower half of the frame worked). The same flaw once made an automatic verdict print false on a run that had actually succeeded.

hazards.hazard: The game can take foreground focus on its own, intermittently
hazards.notes: One run: focus jumped to the game ~20 s in. The next 110 s run: never. n=1 each way, so treat EVERY launch as able to take focus. Matters if the user is working on the same machine - on 2026-09-16 the user was operating a physical engraver in another program. Log the foreground PROCESS NAME per sample (never window titles) to make this checkable.

hazards.hazard: Capture method: PrintWindow was used here and has not been validated for non-moving states
hazards.notes: PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) on the game's own window captured correct, changing frames during the intros and gameplay, and does not take focus. UNIVERSAL guidance warns PrintWindow can serve a STALE cached frame when a game stops presenting (paused, menus, loading). Not checked on this game for those states; prefer BitBlt from the screen DC where the window can be in front.

hazards.hazard: The graphics plugin can silently go stale on deploy
hazards.notes: The game build writes darknessrecomp.exe and rexruntime.dll to the game's out/build folder, but rexgpu-xenos.dll to the SHARED SDK output folder (E:/condemned-2-vr/src/rexglue-sdk/out/win-amd64/). A deploy step that only copied from the game folder left an older rexgpu-xenos.dll installed for most of 2026-09-16 - all of that day's first live results ran on it. Condemned 2 builds into the same shared folder, so building one project overwrites the other's plugin. Hash-check all three files before trusting a run.

hazards.hazard: Self-close is by process kill, not a graceful quit
hazards.notes: Every automated run so far ended with taskkill /F. No graceful in-game quit route has been mapped. Low risk on a dev build with no save of value, but the in-game quit route is still a missing capability.

hazards.hazard: Pad input silently ignored when the game window is not focused
hazards.notes: n=1 failing run, correlational. The failure looks exactly like 'the route is broken' or 'the new build broke input': no error, the menu simply never advances and the attract trailer starts. Log the foreground process per sample so the cause is visible. See input.api_notes for the SDK option that should remove the dependency.

hazards.hazard: QUICKMAP / QUICKMENU do not yet reach a level
hazards.notes: Both used to kill the process instantly on one of the game's own debug assertions (guest 0x820DFC60 -> DbgBreakPoint, exit 0x80000003, NOTHING in the log). Fixed in the shared SDK so a guest DbgBreakPoint logs and continues. Past it, the run stops on a missing font ('d:\content onts	ext.xfc' -> XamShowDirtyDiscErrorUI) and sits at ~455 MB with nothing drawing. Use the main menu's CHECKPOINTS level select instead until the font question is settled.

hazards.hazard: Focus stealing is intermittent, so a focus change proves nothing
hazards.notes: Across five runs the game took the foreground at launch in some and left it with the launching shell for entire runs in others (n=2 each way). The 2026-09-16 hazard below still stands for INPUT, but 'the foreground changed' must not be read as 'the game grabbed focus'. Record the foreground process name at every sample.

notes: Automation, scored against the five capabilities as of 2026-09-18: (1) self-launch PROVEN; (2) menu to gameplay PROVEN, timing-based, via the virtual pad - and the route now includes the save-notice dialogue (START, A, START); (3) commands MISSING - no console; the QUICKMAP/QUICKMENU ENV route is read but stops on a missing font, and the in-data DevMenu is gated by cheat(); (4) camera PROVEN via the right stick, character movement NOT TESTED; (5) self-close by process kill only, graceful quit NOT MAPPED.
The first real-time 3D in this build and the look-stick result are documented with screenshots in the-darkness-vr/dev-archive/milestone-captures/.
Untried and cheapest: the main menu's CHECKPOINTS entry is a retail level select, needing no ENV switch and no patch.

The fonts and models are packed inside Content/Xdf/*.XDF, not loose on the disc. The disc dump is byte-perfect (498 files, 0 missing, 0 size mismatches), so a missing-file error means 'not precached', never 'bad rip'.

disproved.claim: Setting SHOW_DEVELOPMENT=1 and SHOW_CONFIDENTIAL=1 in EnvironmentXbox.cfg opens the built-in DevMenu
disproved.result: No. With both keys set, X (GUI_BUTTON2) twice and Space on the main menu changed nothing. The DevMenu, free camera (dbgcam_*), noclip and god-mode are all present in retail CubeWnd.xcr and in the executable, but every entrance is gated by cheat(...) and that gate did not open.

disproved.claim: EnvironmentXbox.cfg works when placed beside the host executable
disproved.result: No. Host-side it is ignored entirely - a QUICKMAP run there was indistinguishable from no file. It must go in the GAME's disc root (the Assets junction, guest D:\), i.e. E:	he-darkness\game-files\.

disproved.claim: QUICKMENU=DevMenu boots straight into the built-in developer menu
disproved.result: No. It fails exactly like QUICKMAP: the same missing font (d:\content onts	ext.xfc) and the same XamShowDirtyDiscErrorUI, with nothing drawing. Every ENV quick-start route skips the front-end GUI precache, so none of them are usable shortcuts. Separately, cheat() - the gate on every dev-menu entrance - was found to be an empty stub that tests nothing, so no config line can open the menu at all; it needs a code hook on sub_8236F300.
